description: Stand up the Family Pulse application skeleton, PostgreSQL schema, Plaid integration (Transactions + Liabilities sync), transfer detection engine, and development infrastructure. This is the data plumbing layer — no UI. Exit criteria: real family transaction data queryable in the database.

timing.gatingCondition: Plaid access tokens available (already onboarded). Docker available for dev PostgreSQL.

principles: Data integrity first — every Plaid response validated before storage
Idempotent sync — re-running sync never creates duplicates
Transfer detection runs automatically post-sync, before any downstream consumers
Dev environment must be isolated from production data
Test coverage from day one — Plaid API stewardship requires verified correctness

SECRETS NEVER LEAVE THE SERVER — access tokens, API keys, .env values, and sensitive DB columns (items.access_token) are never logged, never returned in API responses, never included in LLM prompts, and never sent to the browser. This is a hardcoded project-wide invariant enforced by code review and test coverage.

techStack.database: PostgreSQL (docker-compose for dev, erebor instance for prod)
techStack.testing: Jest for unit + integration tests, Plaid sandbox for API integration

userStories.title: Project scaffold and dev environment
acceptanceCriteria: Node/Express project initialized with package.json, .env.example, .gitignore
docker-compose.yml provides PostgreSQL 16 instance for local development
PM2 ecosystem config file created
deploy/deploy.sh follows worktree checkout pattern from sibling apps
Server starts and responds to GET /pulse/api/health with { status: 'ok' }
CLAUDE.md created with project conventions
userStories.testStrategy: Health endpoint test, server startup test, docker-compose up validates DB connectivity

userStories.title: PostgreSQL schema initialization
acceptanceCriteria: All core tables created: items, accounts, transactions, categories, category_rules, budgets, budget_periods, planning_goals, savings_signals, magic_actions_log, anomalies, import_runs
Migration system: numbered SQL files in db/migrations/, applied in order
Seed script for default categories (uncategorized, income, transfer)
Schema supports all transfer_type values: inter_account, cc_payment, 529_contribution, btc_savings
Indexes on transactions(account_id, date), transactions(plaid_transaction_id)
Foreign key constraints enforced
userStories.testStrategy: Migration idempotency test (run twice, no errors). Schema validation tests confirm all tables, columns, and constraints exist.

userStories.title: Plaid Items and Accounts sync
acceptanceCriteria: Plaid client initialized from env vars (PLAID_CLIENT_ID, PLAID_SECRET, PLAID_ENV)
API endpoint POST /pulse/api/admin/sync triggers full sync for all Items
Items table stores: access_token (plain text, protected by erebor full-disk encryption), item_id, institution_id, institution_name, status, error_code, token_last_used_at
Accounts table stores: plaid account_id, name, official_name, type, subtype, mask, current_balance, available_balance, iso_currency_code
Account balances updated on every sync
Handles Plaid API errors gracefully: ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMIT, etc.
Access tokens never logged or returned in API responses
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for response parsing and error handling. Integration tests with Plaid sandbox. Verify access tokens excluded from all log output.

userStories.title: Transaction sync engine (cron-based)
acceptanceCriteria: Uses Plaid /transactions/sync (cursor-based) for incremental updates
Stores sync cursor per Item for resumable sync
Handles added, modified, and removed transactions from sync response
Transactions stored with: plaid_transaction_id, account_id, amount, date, authorized_date, merchant_name, name, category (Plaid), pending, iso_currency_code, raw_json
Deduplication by plaid_transaction_id (upsert pattern)
Pending transactions updated when they post
Cron-scheduled sync: morning (6 AM) and evening (8 PM) via node-cron
Manual sync trigger via POST /pulse/api/admin/sync and npm run sync
Sync status tracked: last_sync_at timestamp per Item, logged on completion
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for transaction upsert logic, cursor management, and dedup. Integration test with Plaid sandbox sync endpoint. Cron schedule validation test.

userStories.title: Liabilities sync for credit accounts
acceptanceCriteria: Plaid /liabilities/get called for credit-type Items
Credit card details stored: last_statement_balance, last_statement_date, minimum_payment_amount, next_payment_due_date, last_payment_amount
Liabilities data linked to existing accounts table via plaid account_id
Sync runs as part of the main sync cycle (after accounts, before transfer detection)
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for liabilities response parsing. Integration test confirming credit account details persist correctly.

userStories.title: Transfer detection engine
acceptanceCriteria: Runs automatically after transaction sync completes
Detects inter-account transfers: same absolute amount ±$1, opposite signs, within 3-day window, across linked accounts
Detects credit card payments: payee pattern match (e.g., 'CHASE CARD', 'CITI PAYMENT') + amount matching against credit accounts
Detects 529 contributions: merchant/payee pattern match (configurable in category_rules)
Detects BTC savings: merchant pattern match (Coinbase, Swan, Strike, etc.)
Sets is_transfer=true and transfer_type on matched transactions
Paired transfers linked via transfer_pair_id
Transfer detection is idempotent — re-running does not create duplicate flags
All is_transfer=true transactions excluded from budget/spend calculations by default
userStories.testStrategy: Comprehensive unit tests: paired transfer matching (exact, fuzzy ±$1, edge cases), CC payment detection, 529/BTC pattern matching. Test with synthetic transaction sets covering all transfer types. Idempotency test.

userStories.title: Admin CLI and logging
acceptanceCriteria: npm run sync — triggers manual full sync from command line
npm run accounts — lists all accounts with balances
npm run status — shows last sync time, transaction count, any Item errors
Structured logging (JSON format) with log levels: info, warn, error
Sensitive data (access tokens, full account numbers) never appears in logs
Plaid API call logging: endpoint, status, duration (no request/response bodies)
userStories.testStrategy: CLI smoke tests. Log output validation: confirm no sensitive data leaks in log output across all log levels.

high: Secrets leaking to LLM prompts, logs, API responses, or browser — hardcoded invariant: access tokens, API keys, .env values, and items.access_token column never leave server-side code paths. Enforced by dedicated test suite.
medium: Transfer detection false positives — paired matching may incorrectly flag legitimate transactions as transfers
Plaid rate limits during initial historical sync — may need backoff/retry logic
Docker dev environment must not accidentally connect to production Plaid credentials
low: PostgreSQL version differences between dev (Docker) and prod (erebor)
node-cron timezone handling for daily sync schedule

preFlightChecklist: Confirm Plaid sandbox credentials available for testing (separate from production)
Confirm erebor PostgreSQL version for Docker image parity
Confirm nginx mountpoint /pulse/ is available on erebor
